newsitem.title: USA: Cosby murder case witnesses unreliable, lawyer says.
newsitem.headline: Cosby murder case witnesses unreliable, lawyer says.

text.p: A former lawyer for the man accused of murdering comedian Bill Cosby's son Ennis said on Monday the prosecution's case was based on unreliable witnesses and criminals.

"They're horrible, unreliable, of dubious credibility," said Darren Kavinoky, the attorney originally hired to defend Mikhail Markhasev on charges of murdering Ennis Cosby last January on a Los Angeles freeway.

"I don't want to get myself into a slander situation, but it will give the jury a lot to chew on," added Kavinoky, who dropped out of the case in May when the 18-year-old Ukrainian immigrant's family said they could no longer afford to retain him. However, he said he has followed events closely since then.
Lawyers in the case have been ordered not to talk about it amid media speculation that the evidence against Markhasev might not be as strong as originally claimed by police.
News reports said the only direct witness to the moments before the killing failed to pick Markhasev out of a lineup and police did not get usable fingerprints off the murder weapon.
Markhasev pleaded not guilty to murdering Ennis Cosby, 27, during a botched robbery when Cosby had pulled his car onto an emergency lane to fix a flat tire.
Kavinoky spoke to reporters after a hearing in the Santa Monica courthouse where the case was once again put back.
The hearing was to have been to inform Judge David Perez of the status of the case and set a trial date. Instead, Perez set a date of Oct. 10 for another status hearing.

Markhasev's court-appointed lawyer Hank Hill told Perez he was not ready to set a trial date because he had "several thousand pages of materials" to wade through, in addition to 60 to 80 audio and video tapes, some of which ran two hours.
Outside of court, Hill told reporters he was looking into anything that might affect the credibility of the prosecution witnesses and Kavinoky said there was plenty to find.
"There is going to be a lot of folks coming up to the (witness) stand with a lot of problems, problems of credibility, veracity," Kavinoky said.
Without naming anyone, Kavinoky claimed some prosecution witnesses had been involved in drug taking and theft and had "lapses of honesty."

In addition to those who lacked credibility for various reasons, Kavinoky cited what he called the government's "star witness," a woman friend of Ennis Cosby who responded to his phone call for help in fixing a flat tire and who may have witnessed the murder.
"Not only did she fail to pick out Markhasev in a police line-up, she identified everybody but Markhasev," he said.
